messages:
liam: heads-up — seeing a regression in the EU canary after last night's rollout, lots of heatmaps + sparklines slow to paint
liam: LCP for some dashboards jumped from ~200ms -> ~1.1s around 2026-03-20T15:12Z
liam: perf link: https://redwood.internal/observability/console/perf?env=canary (look for the 3/20 spike)
maria: repro'd locally with the canary bundle. open org with ~40 charts and first-paint stalls
maria: devtools flame shows main thread dominated by parse/execute work when telemetry sampler boots
sachin: we enabled telemetry-eager-init=true in rollout yesterday so sampler initializes at top-level import
sachin: that moved telemetry-client into the root client bundle instead of lazy widget import
ashley: bundle diff (canary vs main): telemetry-client +50KB gz, embedlib +18KB gz — gz size masks parse/exec penalty
ashley: size output:
```
+ telemetry-client.min.js  +50KB gz
+ embedlib.min.js         +18KB gz
```
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary 2026-03-20T15:12Z -> eu 10%, us 5%
maria: flipping TELEMETRY_EAGER=false locally unblocks hydration and charts paint normally
maria: reverting eager import on canary removes the spike in my repro
liam: also seeing KV cache evict-rate ~3x during the same window — maybe TTL/size or churn from prefetch
ashley: note: prefetch window was widened last week (prefetch-window up 1.5x). that increases parallel chunk parse and can amplify eager imports
sachin: hypothesized sequence: prefetch change -> more parallel chunk parsing -> telemetry eager import executes earlier across many widgets -> main-thread contention
ashley: short-term mitigation: revert telemetry eager-init on canary, observe. if evictions persist, roll back prefetch-window concurrently
maria: low-risk code change: replace top-level `import 'telemetry-client'` with an async dynamic import guarded by a feature flag so parse is deferred until widget mount
maria: snippet I used:
```js
if (window.__ENABLE_TELEMETRY_EAGER__) {
  import('./telemetry-client').then(m => m.init())
} else {
  async function mountChart() {
    const t = await import('./telemetry-client')
    t.init()
    renderChart()
  }
}
```
sachin: opening PR for lazy-load + flag: https://git.redwood/console/pull/4199 (WIP)
liam: ops asks: 1) temporary kvcache capacity bump on canary, 2) add telemetry.parse_ms metric to correlate parse cost
ashley: +1 to parse metric. I have a local timer for telemetry.parse_ms, will push after PR merges
eng-sre: acknowledged. provisioning +25% kvcache memory on canary nodes for 2 hours, ETA ~5min
eng-sre: kvcache bump live, monitoring evict-rate + latency now
liam: plan: revert telemetry eager -> test with kvcache bump -> if perf improves hold prefetch change from continuing rollout
maria: I'll smoke test canary post-merge and report results here
sachin: will add unit tests for flag behavior and the parse timer in PR today
ashley: also worth adding a short-sampling experiment: enable eager on a tiny set of clients with parse timer on, to measure head-to-head impact before wide rollout
liam: agreed. if PR stabilizes canary we can gate the telemetry change behind a rollout ramp with parse metrics required for next step
maria: incident note: https://redwood.ops/incidents/2026-03-20-console-canary-regression (short blurb + links)
ashley: action items:
- @sachin finish PR for telemetry lazy-load + add telemetry.parse_ms
- @maria smoke-test canary after merge
- @eng-sre temporary kvcache bump + monitor
- @infra review prefetch-window rollback if needed
liam: keep updates here. if we don't see improvement we'll convene a rollback sync. :thumbsup:
